Introduction

Three Horizons

  1. The question

    What isn't working in how work runs today?

  2. The question

    Ten years from now, if we chose it: what does good work look like?

  3. The question

    What is already changing?

More
  • In one line Three patterns at once: what is fading, what is growing, and the messy middle.
  • Where it comes from Bill Sharpe, with the International Futures Forum.
  • The order Horizon 1, then 3, then 2. The middle comes last.
  • Three mindsets Manager protects what runs (H1). Entrepreneur finds the opening (H2). Visionary speaks from values (H3).

Reading the chart

  • Up the side: how common a way of working is. Higher, more people work that way.
  • Along the bottom: time, from today out to years from now.
  • Each line is one way of working, fading, rising, or passing through.
  • Horizon 1, how work runs today
  • Horizon 3, a future we would choose
  • Horizon 2, the messy middle
  • Each sticky is an example, placed on the line it belongs to.

Horizon 1

How work runs today

  • Common now, fading. The way work is done and valued today.
    • The wage gap. Workers get 52.8% of what US businesses produce, the lowest share on record. US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Q2 2026.
    • The 40-hour week at a desk, five days a week.
  • What we take for granted: how we are paid, measured and hired.
    • Paid: by the hour or the salary, not by what we make possible.
    • Measured: hours logged, output counted, the annual review.
    • Hired: a resume, a degree, a job title.

What isn't working in how work runs today?

Horizon 3

A future we would choose

  • Rare now, growing. Bits of it already exist.
    • What if the time AI saves came back to the people doing the work?
    • A four-day week: the same pay, one day less.
  • Pockets of the future: places already working the way we want.
    • Mondragon, Spain: a network of worker-owned co-ops that back each other.
    • Marcora Law, Italy: workers can buy the firm that failed them and run it as a co-op.
    • Community AI: local AI on discarded office workstations.

Ten years from now, if we chose it: what does good work look like?

Horizon 2

The messy middle

  • Where new tools and rules show up. AI lands here first.
    • A company AI policy. Raised at both of Kyle Hobson’s workshops.
    • AI note-takers in every meeting.
    • AI training paid for by the employer.
  • Plaster or stepping stone? A plaster patches how work runs today. A stepping stone moves us toward the future we want.
    • Plaster: AI bought to cut staff, so fewer people carry the same work.
    • Stepping stone: AI the team picks to drop busywork, and the hours saved stay with them.
    • Could be either: a note-taker that frees up time, or one that keeps a record of everyone.

Horizon 2 the messy middle

Marked green

  • Health breakthrough
  • Democratization of development

Marked red

Unmarked

Horizon 3 a future we would choose

  • Easier to change
  • More time with friends and family
  • Increased access to healthcare
  • Resource management that enables abundance and sustainable resource sharing
  • Less suffering
  • Creative renaissance
  • Digital experiences without giving up your digital data
